title: Classification of organic compounds
notes: **Open-chain compounds.** Aliphatic compounds have open carbon chains — straight-chain (n-butane) or branched-chain (isobutane) — and may be saturated or unsaturated.
**Cyclic compounds.** Closed-ring compounds divide into carbocycles (alicyclic like cyclohexane; aromatic like benzene) and heterocycles (furan, pyridine) that contain non-carbon atoms in the ring.
**Functional group classes.** Compounds are grouped by their functional group: halides (—X), alcohols (—OH), aldehydes (—CHO), ketones (>C=O), carboxylic acids (—COOH) and amines (—NH₂).
**Saturated vs unsaturated.** Compounds with only single C—C bonds are saturated; those with double or triple bonds are unsaturated and decolourise bromine water.
**Why classification matters.** Members of one class show similar chemical properties, so classifying a compound immediately predicts its reactions and its name.
